from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: High-Dimensional Vector Spaces", [
            "Words and pixels live in vector spaces.",
            "Proximity in these spaces denotes semantic meaning.",
            "This enables math to relate concepts accurately."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Load assets
        word_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/words.svg")
        pixel_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixels.svg")
        
        # Display vector space (using icons as points)
        pt1 = word_icon.copy()
        pt2 = word_icon.copy()
        self.place_at_grid(pt1, 'A2', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(pt2, 'B5', scale_factor=0.3)
        
        vector_arrow = Arrow(start=pt1.get_center(), end=pt2.get_center(), color="#33FF57")
        scene_objects = VGroup(pt1, pt2, vector_arrow)
        
        self.place_in_area(scene_objects, 'A2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(vector_arrow, 'A4', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(pt1), Create(pt2), Create(vector_arrow))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Dot cloud representing space
        dot_cloud = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.03, color=BLUE) for _ in range(30)])
        for dot in dot_cloud:
            dot.move_to(np.array([float(np.random.uniform(-1, 1)), float(np.random.uniform(-1, 1)), 0.0]))
        self.place_in_area(dot_cloud, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_cloud))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00") # Highlighting proximity

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show math equation relating concepts
        eq = MathTex(r"sim(\vec{v}_{word}, \vec{v}_{pixel})", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(eq, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Diffusion adds noise to destroy original images.",
            "The forward process maps data to chaos.",
            "Reverse diffusion learns to undo this noise.",
            "We step-by-step refine noise into clarity.",
            "This math recovers structure from randomness."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Artist: The Diffusion Process", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        photo = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/photograph.svg")
        noise = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/noise.svg")
        
        # Initial placement
        self.place_in_area(photo, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Noise dots for simulation
        noise_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=np.random.normal(0, 0.5, 3), color=WHITE, radius=0.03) for _ in range(200)])

        # Math formula
        formula = MathTex(r"x_t = \sqrt{1-\beta_t}x_{t-1} + \sqrt{\beta_t}\epsilon", font_size=32)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF33A1"))
        self.add(photo)
        self.play(Transform(photo, noise))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        # Using noise icon here
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33A1FF"))
        self.play(Transform(noise, photo))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF33"))
        self.place_in_area(noise_dots, "B1", "E3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(noise_dots))
        self.play(FadeOut(noise_dots))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF8833"))
        self.place_in_area(formula, "C4", "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.add(photo)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Putting it All Together", [
            "The model starts with pure static noise.",
            "CLIP provides feedback on the current sketch.",
            "The diffusion process refines the image step-by-step."
        ])
        
        # Define elements with assets
        noise_img = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/noise.svg")
        clip_img = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/clip.svg")
        diff_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.5, color=GREEN)
        image_rect = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.5, color=WHITE)
        
        noise_label = Text("Noise", font_size=18)
        clip_label = Text("CLIP", font_size=18)
        diff_label = Text("Diffusion", font_size=18)
        image_label = Text("Image", font_size=18)
        
        # Groupings
        noise_group = VGroup(noise_img, noise_label).arrange(DOWN)
        clip_group = VGroup(clip_img, clip_label).arrange(DOWN)
        diff_group = VGroup(diff_box, diff_label).arrange(DOWN)
        image_group = VGroup(image_rect, image_label).arrange(DOWN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GREY)
        self.place_at_grid(noise_group, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(noise_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(clip_group, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        arrow_clip = Arrow(start=noise_group.get_right(), end=clip_group.get_left(), color=BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(clip_group), Create(arrow_clip))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(diff_group, "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(image_group, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        arrow_diff = Arrow(start=clip_group.get_bottom(), end=diff_group.get_top(), color=GREEN)
        arrow_res = Arrow(start=diff_group.get_left(), end=image_group.get_right(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(diff_group), Create(arrow_diff), FadeIn(image_group), Create(arrow_res))
        
        # Iterative indicator
        loop_arrow = CurvedArrow(start_point=image_group.get_left() + LEFT*0.5, end_point=noise_group.get_left() + LEFT*0.5, angle=TAU/4, color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(loop_arrow))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Text-to-Image AI: Diffusion and CLIP Explained
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic background in linear algebra and calculus

sections.title: Introduction: The Creative Loop
sections.content: A 30-second overview defining text-to-image generation as a bridge between language and visual space. We introduce the two protagonists: CLIP (the guide) and Diffusion (the artist).
sections.example: Inputting 'A fluffy corgi wearing a space suit' and seeing it materialize from static noise.

sections.title: Prerequisites: High-Dimensional Vector Spaces
sections.content: Briefly introduce 'Embedding Spaces' (45 seconds). Explain how words and pixels are converted into numerical coordinates where proximity denotes semantic similarity.
sections.example: Visualizing 'Cat' and 'Dog' as two points close to each other in a 512-dimensional graph, while 'Robot' is further away.

sections.title: The Navigator: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training)
sections.content: Explain CLIP as a 'Matching Game' (60 seconds). It maps text descriptions and images into the same space, calculating similarity scores to tell the model if it's on the right track.
sections.example: A sliding scale gauge animation showing how the AI's current sketch aligns (matches) with the prompt 'corgi' vs 'cat'.

sections.title: The Artist: The Diffusion Process (Math Focus)
sections.content: Explain the Forward (noise addition) and Reverse (denoising) processes (90 seconds). Use the Gaussian noise function representation: x_t = sqrt(1-β_t)x_{t-1} + sqrt(β_t)ε. Show the transition from pure static to clear edges.
sections.example: A frame-by-frame animation of a snowy television screen gradually clarifying into a high-definition image of an astronaut.

sections.title: Synthesis: Putting it All Together
sections.content: Show the feedback loop (45 seconds): The model starts with noise, CLIP provides a 'gradient' (direction of change) based on the prompt, and the Diffusion model subtracts the predicted noise step-by-step.
sections.example: A flow chart showing: [Prompt] -> [CLIP Score] -> [Denoising Step] -> [Refined Image] -> Repeat 50 times.

sections.title: Conclusion and Future Outlook
sections.content: Summary of how math transforms chaos (noise) into meaning (art) (30 seconds).
sections.example: Comparing a simple line drawing vs. a sophisticated 4K generated portrait to highlight the model's potential.

storyboard.title: Introduction: The Creative Loop
lecture_lines: Text-to-image AI bridges language and visual space.
CLIP acts as our knowledgeable creative guide.
Diffusion models function as our talented artist.
Together they turn prompts into beautiful images.
animations: Show Text "Text-to-image AI" in center (#FFFFFF).
Fade in (CLIP icon) with label in blue (#33A1FF).
Fade in (Diffusion icon) with label in pink (#FF33A1).
Animate a cycle connection between CLIP and Diffusion.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: High-Dimensional Vector Spaces
lecture_lines: Words and pixels live in vector spaces.
Proximity in these spaces denotes semantic meaning.
This enables math to relate concepts accurately.
animations: Display 2D vector space with multiple points (#33FF57) representing.
Highlight proximity between two related points with color #FFFF00.
Show math equation relating two concept vectors representing.

storyboard.title: The Navigator: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training)
lecture_lines: CLIP matches text and images together perfectly.
It calculates similarity scores for alignment.
This guides the model towards the target.
animations: Show text block and image block side-by-side.
Draw a connection line (#33A1FF) between and the image block.
Display a dynamic numerical similarity score.

storyboard.title: The Artist: The Diffusion Process (Math Focus)
lecture_lines: Diffusion adds noise to destroy original images.
The forward process maps data to chaos.
Reverse diffusion learns to undo this noise.
We step-by-step refine noise into clarity.
This math recovers structure from randomness.
animations: Show a clear image transitioning to noisy state (#FF33A1).
Show noisy image transitioning back to clear image.
Draw a noise distribution bar plot.
Display iterative refinement steps with timestamps.
Final image appears as clear structure from noise.

storyboard.title: Synthesis: Putting it All Together
lecture_lines: The model starts with pure static noise.
CLIP provides feedback on the current sketch.
The diffusion process refines the image step-by-step.
animations: Show block on left, on top.
Show refined image output block on the right.
Animate iterative flow between and blocks.

storyboard.title: Conclusion and Future Outlook
lecture_lines: Math transforms chaos into meaningful art.
From static noise emerges structured beauty.
AI unlocks infinite creative possibilities today.
animations: Display list of key concepts in #FFFFFF alongside.
Animate expansion of concepts into infinite space.
Display final text #FFFFFF \"Ready to build?\" with.
